title: A specialty practice spends 13 staff-hours a week proving medically necessary care to insurers
job: Get medication/procedure approved with minimum clinician/staff effort and without delaying care.
trigger: Order or prescription triggers prior authorization or denial.
surfaceComplaint: We keep resubmitting the same facts in different payer forms.
mechanism: Each payer/product encodes different evidence requirements. Existing chart information must be repeatedly located, transformed, submitted, tracked and appealed.

workflow.friction: chart not packaged to payer criteria

existingSpend.amount: 40% of surveyed physicians report dedicated staff

economics.painCostNote: AMA reports about 40 PAs and 13 physician/staff hours per physician each week.

distribution.acquisition: Start with one specialty and one high-volume authorization class.

intervention.notBuildYet: No autonomous clinical assertions or appeals.

experiment.artifactRequest: de-identified PA packets + criteria + timestamps + outcomes
experiment.success: ≥40% staff-time reduction, no increase in submission errors, shorter turnaround
experiment.kill: payer variation or compliance cost overwhelms saved labor

claims.text: AMA's 2026 survey reports 40 prior authorizations per physician per week on average.
AMA reports 13 hours of physician/staff time per week spent on prior authorization.
The first product should narrow to one high-volume authorization class.
